parsed.impact: described.rs `parse`, the `RULES` prompt, the response schema and `KINDS` are shared with the add path (US-10-02/03); the add cases were left in the set, the schema now requires "event", and the new "change" prompt rules could make a real model misread an add as a change (TC-10-19 is the only guard). main.rs now takes the model's answer and the looked-up names while an event's details are open (DEC-231), which changes when a described add opens its window; `Editor::follow_start` and `Regional` formatting are reused by `Change::apply`. `pub(super)` test helpers were widened in description_guests_tests.rs.

findings.text: crates/app/src/main.rs:2003 — `selected` is captured only when the box gains focus. Scenario: details of A are open, the user clicks the box, then presses Esc (the Esc handling in `shortcuts` closes the details even while a text field has focus, main.rs:964), types "przesuń standup na 10" and sends. `selected` is still A, so the editor opens A instead of matching "standup", and the name is ignored. The same happens after an add or a "no event" answer, because `selected` is cleared only in `described_change`. → At Send, also check that `self.dialog` is still that event's details (`same_event`), otherwise drop `selected`. Or take `selected` from the dialog at Send time.

crates/app/src/main.rs:2036 — `self.matches` is cleared only on GoneTo, Send or a pick. If the user opens another dialog or the cache changes, the list reappears when the dialog closes, holding stale `Event` copies (`matches.events[i].clone()` is passed straight to `change_event`, not re-read from `self.events`). → Re-resolve the picked event via `same_event` against `self.events` as the `selected` branch does, and clear `matches` when a dialog opens.

crates/app/src/description.rs:293 — While the list is showing and no text field has focus, Enter and arrows are consumed app-wide (`consume_key`) and Esc closes the list too, e.g. Enter on a focused grid event. → Gate on the list or box having focus, or clear `matches` when focus goes elsewhere.

crates/core/src/described.rs:176 — `matching` runs over all of `self.events`, including events of calendars the user has hidden in the side panel. `side_panel::shown` filters those out of the views, so the user can be offered an event they cannot see. → Filter on `side_panel::shown` or the calendar's visibility, or confirm that is intended.

crates/core/src/described.rs:176 — Matching in both directions (DEC-229, `within(&title,&name)`) is broad. A lone event titled "Spotkanie" fits "spotkanie z Anią" and, if it is the only match, opens straight away although a more specific "Spotkanie z Anią" may be a different event. → Consider ranking or preferring the longer overlap, or accept it and say so in the DEC.

crates/app/src/main.rs:2170 — When the target cannot be edited and its details are already open (DEC-230), nothing visibly happens, because the description stays and no message is shown. → Optionally flash a message, or note it in the manual check.

crates/core/src/described.rs:1 — The module doc line is 149 characters, so it was not reflowed after the edit. The doc comment on `Change::apply` should also mention that title, guests and Meet are not applied.

crates/core/src/described_cases.json:1 — The change cases' answers are labelled as gemma4:e4b output, but the "event" values for "Kawa z Bartkiem" and "meeting with Anna" differ in style from the others and cannot be verified. The fake model only tests the app's parsing, not the prompt, so the 95 % / 80 % result against the real model rests on the manual TC-10-19.
